import os
import re
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score

# Set random seeds for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

print("Loading data...")
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_test_2.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_sample_submission_2.csv")

print(f"Train shape: {train_df.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test_df.shape}")

# Check for class column in test (it may not exist)
print(f"Test columns: {test_df.columns.tolist()}")
print(f"Train columns: {train_df.columns.tolist()}")


# Convert all 'before' values to string and handle NaN/None
def safe_to_str(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return ""
    return str(x).strip()


train_df["before_str"] = train_df["before"].apply(safe_to_str)
test_df["before_str"] = test_df["before"].apply(safe_to_str)

# Build class label mapping from training data only
class_labels = sorted(train_df["class"].unique()) if "class" in train_df.columns else []
class_to_idx = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(class_labels)} if class_labels else {None: 0}

print(f"Number of classes: {len(class_labels)}")
print(f"Class labels: {class_labels}")

# Split training data into train and validation (by row, not by id for simplicity)
# Use stratified split if class exists
if len(class_labels) > 1:
    train_temp, val_df = train_test_split(
        train_df, test_size=0.1, random_state=42, stratify=train_df["class"]
    )
else:
    train_temp, val_df = train_test_split(train_df, test_size=0.1, random_state=42)

print(f"Train temp size: {len(train_temp)}")
print(f"Validation size: {len(val_df)}")

# Build text-to-class inference map from train_temp ONLY
print("Building text-to-class inference map...")
text_to_class_map = {}
for _, row in train_temp.iterrows():
    before_str = row["before_str"]
    cls = row["class"]
    if before_str in text_to_class_map:
        text_to_class_map[before_str].append(cls)
    else:
        text_to_class_map[before_str] = [cls]

# Convert to most frequent class per text
for text, class_list in text_to_class_map.items():
    text_to_class_map[text] = Counter(class_list).most_common(1)[0][0]

print(f"Text-to-class map size: {len(text_to_class_map)} entries")


# Function to infer class from text
def infer_class(input_text):
    """Infer class for input text using training-derived mapping"""
    return text_to_class_map.get(input_text, None)


# Function to predict using pattern matching
def predict_after(input_text, input_class, patterns, mode_outputs):
    """
    Predict normalized text using pattern matching with multiple fallback strategies
    """
    # Infer class from text if not provided
    if input_class is None:
        inferred_class = infer_class(input_text)
        if inferred_class is not None:
            input_class = inferred_class

    # Get fallback for this class
    fallback = mode_outputs.get(input_class, input_text)

    # Try exact match
    key = (input_class, input_text)
    if key in patterns:
        candidates = patterns[key]
        if candidates:
            return candidates[0]

    # Try prefix match (first 3 chars)
    if len(input_text) >= 3:
        prefix_key = (input_class, input_text[:3])
        if prefix_key in patterns:
            candidates = patterns[prefix_key]
            if candidates:
                return candidates[0]

    # Try exact word-level match
    words = input_text.split()
    for word in words:
        word_key = (input_class, word)
        if word_key in patterns:
            candidates = patterns[word_key]
            if candidates:
                return candidates[0]

    return fallback


# Build pattern mappings per class
class_patterns = defaultdict(list)

for cls in class_labels:
    cls_mask = train_temp["class"] == cls
    cls_df = train_temp[cls_mask]

    for _, row in cls_df.iterrows():
        input_text = row["before_str"]
        output_text = row["after"]

        # Store exact match
        class_patterns[(cls, input_text)].append(output_text)

        # Store prefix matches (first 3 chars)
        if len(input_text) >= 3:
            prefix = input_text[:3]
            class_patterns[(cls, prefix)].append(output_text)

        # Store common character n-gram patterns
        words = input_text.split()
        for word in words[:5]:  # Limit to first 5 words per example
            class_patterns[(cls, word)].append(output_text)

print(f"Pattern mappings built: {len(class_patterns)} entries")

# Fallback: most common output per class
class_mode_outputs = {}
for cls in class_labels:
    cls_df = train_temp[train_temp["class"] == cls]
    mode = cls_df["after"].mode()
    if len(mode) > 0:
        class_mode_outputs[cls] = mode.iloc[0]
    else:
        class_mode_outputs[cls] = ""

print(f"Class fallback mappings: {len(class_mode_outputs)}")


# Generate predictions on test set
print("\nGenerating test predictions...")
test_predictions = []

for idx, row in test_df.iterrows():
    input_text = row["before_str"]
    sentence_id = row["sentence_id"]
    token_id = row["token_id"]

    # Construct ID as required by submission format
    id_str = f"{int(sentence_id)}_{int(token_id)}"

    # Test set doesn't have class column, infer using text_to_class_map
    input_class = None  # Will be inferred inside predict_after

    pred = predict_after(input_text, input_class, class_patterns, class_mode_outputs)

    if pd.isna(pred) or pred is None:
        pred = input_text

    test_predictions.append({"id": id_str, "after": pred})

# Convert to DataFrame
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(test_predictions)

# Ensure submission directory exists
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Save submission
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

print(f"\n=== Submission Summary ===")
print(f"Total predictions: {len(submission_df)}")
print(f"Submission shape: {submission_df.shape}")
print(f"Column names: {submission_df.columns.tolist()}")
print(f"Sample predictions:")
print(submission_df.head(10))

# Validate on held-out validation set (calculate metrics)
print("\n=== Validation on Hold-out Set ===")
val_preds = []
for idx, row in val_df.iterrows():
    input_text = row["before_str"]
    # Use class inference (same logic as test) instead of actual class labels
    input_class = infer_class(input_text)
    pred = predict_after(input_text, input_class, class_patterns, class_mode_outputs)
    val_preds.append(pred)

# Get actual values from validation set
actual_val = (
    val_df["after"].values if "after" in val_df.columns else val_df["after"].tolist()
)

# Calculate accuracy
try:
    val_accuracy = accuracy_score(val_preds, actual_val)
    print(f"Validation Accuracy (pattern matching): {val_accuracy:.6f}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Could not compute validation accuracy with sklearn: {e}")
    # Fallback: manual count
    correct = sum(
        1 for p, a in zip(val_preds, actual_val) if str(p) == str(a) and pd.notna(a)
    )
    total = len(val_preds)
    val_accuracy = correct / total if total > 0 else 0
    print(f"Validation Accuracy (manual): {val_accuracy:.6f}")

print(f"\nFinal Validation Accuracy: {val_accuracy:.6f}")
